A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WebOrganizer study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite layout changes and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classifier evaluations, language-model training experiments, domain-mixture analyses and downstream results in Tables 1–2 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds predicted domain mixtures for additional tasks in Appendix D and Figure 8.

M1.justification: The topic/format taxonomies, two-stage classifier distillation, adaptive RegMix search, product-mixture selection and integration with quality filters remain unchanged. The additional tasks use the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds HumanEval, MBPP, MATH and Natural Questions as mixture-prediction targets alongside MMLU and HellaSwag. This substantially broadens that analysis to coding, mathematical problem solving and open-domain question answering. The final-model benchmark suite remains unchanged.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain the baseline corpus, k-means domains, FineWeb-Edu and DCLM-fasttext, with Data Mixing Laws retained in the regression comparison. Newly discussed related methods are not added as experimental baselines.

E3.justification: The added mixture analyses introduce task-specific protocols: five examples for Natural Questions, three for HumanEval/MBPP and zero for MATH, using correct-solution bits-per-byte. Existing training budgets, splits and downstream evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D and Figure 8 extend the analysis of how preferred topic and format mixtures depend on the target task. Existing two-stage-training, URL-feature and regression-model ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the two random seeds for mixture search and the prompt-order agreement analysis. No new repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 8 adds mixture-preference results: coding targets favor Software Development and Documentation, while Natural Questions strongly favors Entertainment. Existing result tables retain their numerical values; no new final-model accuracy results accompany the added targets.

T1.justification: The NPMI/NMI definitions, topic–format independence assumption, product-mixture equation and KL-regularized adaptive-search mathematics are unchanged. No new theoretical result or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: organizing web data by topic and format, optimizing their mixtures, and complementing quality filtering. The additional analysis supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly argues that rewritten synthetic data can inherit source-domain proportions and therefore could benefit from domain mixing. Existing interpretations of quality filtering and limitations concerning taxonomy bias, prediction noise and scale transfer are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix D documents the loss measure and task-specific prompting counts for the added analyses. Existing classifier settings, RegMix hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware and training-time disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 substantially expands positioning through comparisons with Bai et al.'s topic-based influence selection, Zhang et al.'s diversity-oriented clustering and Held et al.'s LLM-estimated utility. It also adds synthetic-data taxonomy and rephrasing literature, explaining relationships beyond merely adding citations.

P1.justification: v2 adds related-work paragraphs and a short Predicted Mixtures appendix, renumbers Experimental Details from D to E, and makes limited wording and affiliation edits. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column layout to a two-column conference layout, with extensive reflow and figure/table relocation. Appendix Tables 6 and 7 exchange numbering, and a new full-page Figure 8 displays the additional mixture profiles.

improvement.justification: Figure 8 broadens the evidence for task-dependent domain preferences, and the expanded related work better explains the relationship to competing selection and synthetic-data approaches. These are useful, limited gains: the main experiments are unchanged, and the added mixture predictions lack final-model performance validation on the new targets.
